cues.text: A digital-asset desk under bank controls. Meridian Bank (fictional) runs FORGE CUSTODY in its own cloud account. Its payments hub connects through the API; named people decide; an AI agent handles routine corporate settlements under strict terms.
cues.title: Bank · recorded on the running platform

cues.text: Self-hosted inside the bank, with the bank’s people in charge. Deployed with Helm into the bank’s own Kubernetes; the three signing parties can run on separate hosts or accounts, and an HSM can hold the keys.
cues.title: How it fits

cues.text: Connecting the payments hub. The bank’s systems call the API with a key that expires and can be rotated at any time. Transfers carry Travel Rule data in IVMS101 form, so the record exists before the signature does.
cues.title: Chapter 1

cues.text: Rotate the API key, then send with Travel Rule data. Keys expire (API_KEY_TTL_DAYS) and can be rotated by the customer or the operator. Rotation is immediate.
cues.title: Your application

cues.text: The new key works immediately and the old key is refused immediately. There is no overlap window to exploit.
cues.title: Rotation

cues.text: The IVMS101 record was created and checked before the parties signed, then linked to the transaction hash. A transfer missing the data is refused, not signed.
cues.title: Travel Rule first

cues.text: The same kind of transfer without Travel Rule data is refused before any signing, with the reason.
cues.title: Refused

cues.text: Roles and dual control. Every person has exactly one role. The operator who asks for a transfer can never approve it; two approvers must, each with a fresh code.
cues.title: Chapter 2

cues.text: The desk administrator signs in. (Single sign-on through the bank’s identity provider is built and tested; this recording has no provider to connect to.)
cues.title: Sign in

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: Each person has one role. Changes to roles are themselves recorded.
cues.title: People

cues.text: Dual control by default: two approvals. The requester is never counted, and each person decides once.
cues.title: Approval policy

cues.text: The emergency freeze, and a whitelist of addresses the organisation may send to.
cues.title: Safety controls

cues.text: Oscar is an operator: he can ask for a transfer, not approve one.
cues.title: Sign in

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: The sender and recipient details are captured with the request, in the IVMS101 format other providers read, before anything is signed.
cues.title: Travel Rule

cues.text: The last look before money moves. Policy is evaluated when this is confirmed, not before.
cues.title: Review

cues.text: Over 10 ETH, policy requires approval. Nothing is signed; the request waits for two other people.
cues.title: Held

cues.text: Oscar can see his request but the console, and the API behind it, will not let him approve it.
cues.title: Segregation of duties

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: Approver one: Alice, verified with a one-time code.
cues.title: Approval

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: Approver two: Bob. The quorum is met and the stored request runs exactly once.
cues.title: Approval

cues.text: Both decisions are recorded with who, when and how each person was verified. Two of three parties signed; the chain accepted it.
cues.title: Result

cues.text: An AI agent for settlements. The bank lets an AI agent settle routine obligations to one corporate client, in a rand stablecoin, up to R20,000 a payment. Then the desk freezes everything, and the agent stops too.
cues.title: Chapter 3

cues.text: The administrator issues the settlements agent.
cues.title: Sign in

cues.text: A one-time code from the person’s authenticator app. Every sign-in and every approval needs a fresh one.
cues.title: Second factor

cues.text: An agent is a credential that can only pay, within limits a person sets. It is issued here, by an admin.
cues.title: Agents

cues.text: One counterparty, R20,000 a payment, R50,000 a day, seven days. Short expiry is a control in itself.
cues.title: Its terms

cues.text: The agent key is displayed this one time and stored only as a hash. It goes into the AI client’s secret configuration, never into a prompt. (Masked here.)
cues.title: Shown once

cues.text: Connecting an AI client. The MCP server is a small process the AI client starts. It holds only the agent key (and, for Travel Rule payments, the organisation’s own details) and calls the same gateway.
cues.title: Your application

cues.text: MCP is how AI assistants discover and call tools. The server exposes five; only one can move money, and only within the agent’s terms.
cues.title: Model Context Protocol

cues.text: Settle today’s obligation to Harbour Trading Ltd (their wallet is held at Example Exchange): R15,000, reference SET-0931.
cues.speaker: user

cues.text: → get_spending_status()
R15,000 is above the R5,000 Travel Rule threshold, so I’ll include the beneficiary exactly as given: Harbour Trading Ltd, held at Example Exchange.
cues.speaker: agent

cues.text: → send_payment({"token":"tZAR","recipient":"0x33AB722e4Aefb57AC6deAf942B1809e5E4F91f4E","amount":"15000","chain_id":1337,"purpose":"Settlement SET-0931, Harbour Trading","idempotency_key":"set-0931","beneficiary":{"name":"Harbour Trading Ltd","provider":"Example Exchange"}})
Settled R15,000 to Harbour Trading, reference SET-0931, with its Travel Rule record. Confirmed by the platform.
cues.speaker: agent

cues.text: The desk suspects a compromised workstation and freezes the organisation. It stops the console, the API, settlements and agents at once.
cues.title: Emergency freeze

cues.text: Recorded with who, when and why, and sent to the alert channel.
cues.title: Frozen

cues.text: Settle SET-0932: R4,000 to Harbour Trading.
cues.speaker: user

cues.text: → send_payment({"token":"tZAR","recipient":"0x33AB722e4Aefb57AC6deAf942B1809e5E4F91f4E","amount":"4000","chain_id":1337,"purpose":"Settlement SET-0932, Harbour Trading","idempotency_key":"set-0932"})
Refused: the organisation is frozen. I can’t pay anything until an administrator lifts the freeze.
cues.speaker: agent

cues.text: Only an admin can lift it. An approver can freeze but not unfreeze, so a single compromised approver cannot undo a freeze.
cues.title: Lifting the freeze

cues.text: One payment made, one refused because of the freeze, with the reason. The bank can see exactly what the agent did and was stopped from doing.
cues.title: The agent’s record

cues.text: Evidence for audit. What an internal auditor or a regulator would ask for, from the same records the platform uses itself.
cues.title: Chapter 4

cues.text: Every record in IVMS101 form, with its status and the transaction it belongs to.
cues.title: Travel Rule

cues.text: Activity aggregated against reporting thresholds, in rand.
cues.title: Thresholds

cues.text: The platform’s own ledger is compared with the chain. A transfer the chain does not show, or one the ledger does not know, is flagged.
cues.title: Reconciliation

cues.text: Each signed transfer was looked up on the chain by its hash. The result is stored, with who ran it and when, as evidence.
cues.title: Reconciliation

cues.text: Real platform, local chain.
cues.title: What this recording is
